normative_claims.text: The round is a NARROW_REPAIR re-target on an already-repaired S4-R2 product: only the README CLI/Skills split, the --root wording, an isolated focused regression and a conditional integration/release gate are in scope.
main must not be written, tagged or released before a native PROMPT_COMPILE_PASS and a real focused regression receipt exist; the withheld end state is MERGE_READY_HITL_PENDING.
v0.1.0-preview.2 stays public and immutable; a preview.3 distribution must carry a PEP 440 version strictly greater than 0.1.0.
HG-KSEOS is the sole normative control plane; Fabric is a read-only policy contract surface consumed by HGK, never a second writer or credential broker.
The four early ProfileBinding mutants are already closed on the frozen subject; only the version-string grammar stays a deferred P2 observation and must not be re-opened as five live defects.
The maker suite figure measured in a writable checkout and the independent checker PARTIAL verdict are different claim fates and must never be merged into one PASS.

intent.goal: Under HG-KSEOS as the sole control plane, carry the S4-R2 repairs already present on the s4-r2 branch through the two README corrections and an isolated focused regression, then integrate conditionally into main; open a separate release gate for preview.3 only if the owner selects it.
intent.user_expected_outcome: A half-closed round: the README routes CLI and Skills separately, --root is described the way the CLI really behaves, the frozen product passes an isolated affected regression, and main either carries the repairs with a readback or is honestly left at MERGE_READY_HITL_PENDING.
intent.user_expected_experience: An ordinary reader can pick one of two paths and reach a working install or a mounted document pack without believing that a wheel install loads native web skills; preview.2 keeps serving existing users.
explicit_constraints: No 20th schema, no 9th logical skill, no 14th CLI command.
Do not rewrite the frozen s4-r2 product commit, the sealed preview.1/.2 tags or their assets.
The read-only checker subject must never be mutated by a suite run.
Fabric stays a read-only policy consumer; HG-KSEOS stays the only writer-facing control plane.
Five ProfileBinding mutants stay closed; the version grammar stays a deferred P2 observation.
non_goals: S5-S8, GENIE, JIT, SWOF live receivers and the 22 inactive providers.
A full 57-row source crosswalk in PASS state as a precondition for this Beta repair.
Rebuilding the 11 PKG + 10 DOC + skeleton corpus as a second SSOT.
Making PIPD an agent runtime, a security LLM judge or a credential broker.
Re-running a full S0-S4 re-audit after a documentation change.
authorized_mutations: README.md and a small docs smoke test on the admitted candidate branch.
A fast-forward of the approved candidate into main under owner approval.
A new immutable preview tag plus wheel and mount pack, only under a separate owner release approval.
forbidden_mutations: Force-push, tag rewrite, or overwriting a published asset.
Writing into the frozen checker subject or into another profile's skills/plugins/cron.
Printing, copying or committing any credential value.
Widening the admitted write-set without a new requirement.

work_required: bind one sealed Codex writer to the admitted write-set of WO-S4R2M-DOC-CAL-01 and prove the escape is discriminated, not just the in-scope write admitted

dispatch the checker lane on a different model family than the writer and re-derive every decisive figure
reject a maker-authored verdict presented as independent acceptance
satisfy lint, activation and acceptance with zero errors and emit the compiler receipt
keep the rendered thin prompt inside render_policy.max_prompt_chars
admit one requirement per WorkOrder through the typed API and read the binding back
bind the writable_root to the candidate worktree actually used by the writer
create the round board and its swarm root/worker/verifier/synthesizer graph and persist the returned ids
record the named-method route readback and one change proposal, without promoting any method to control authority

journeys.user_goal: A first-time user picks the CLI path and installs the pinned wheel.
journeys.expected_visible_result: The front page states that the wheel carries the Python CLI and 19 schemas and that it does NOT inject the 8 native web skills.
expected_automatic_behavior: the installed wheel is verified against its published digest before any run
doctor reports the schema source it actually resolved
expected_manual_behavior: the user only supplies a venv and a wheel path
negative_behavior: a wheel whose bytes differ from the published digest must refuse, never print OK
failure_recovery: stop at the checksum gate and re-download from the immutable tag

journeys.user_goal: A web user picks the Skills path and mounts the versioned document pack.
journeys.expected_visible_result: The mount guide distinguishes manual document/Knowledge mode from a native skill upload, and native loading stays NOT_RUN unless a host receipt exists.
expected_automatic_behavior: the pack manifest verifies the bytes the user actually received
expected_manual_behavior: the user attaches the markdown and the starter prompt by hand
negative_behavior: a manual attachment must never be reported as a native skill effective-load
failure_recovery: label the path NOT_RUN and keep the manual document route usable

journeys.user_goal: An ordinary reader runs the copy-paste compiler chain twice.
journeys.expected_visible_result: Both runs exit 0 and the six produced artefact digests are identical between passes.
expected_automatic_behavior: the checked-in fixture paths resolve without any placeholder token
a missing source locator is refused with a typed non-zero exit
expected_manual_behavior: the reader substitutes only their own interpreter path
negative_behavior: a missing or tampered source must not be silently compiled into a record
failure_recovery: re-run from a clean scratch root and re-check the digests

journeys.user_goal: A user binds a profile and the duplicate/typed axis mutants are refused.
journeys.expected_visible_result: A legal LITE/STANDARD/ASSURED binding is accepted and every malformed axis form is refused with a typed schema exit.
expected_automatic_behavior: the compiler-issued records stay accepted while the mutants stay refused
expected_manual_behavior: the user supplies only the profile axis set
negative_behavior: turning an unassessed risk into an automatic high-risk approval must never happen
failure_recovery: keep the NEG set and the POS set in the same receipt so neither alone decides

journeys.user_goal: A reader follows the documented --root rules for init, project and export.
journeys.expected_visible_result: The pre-subcommand form works for the compile chain and the subcommand-local form works for project and export, exactly as the documented text says.
expected_automatic_behavior: the documented positive forms all exit 0
an unsupported local form exits non-zero as a typed usage error
expected_manual_behavior: the user copies the documented lines literally
negative_behavior: a claim that every command accepts only the global position must be refuted by the real help output
failure_recovery: fix the prose, never the claim about the CLI

journeys.user_goal: A user wants the new repairs from the public tag.
journeys.expected_visible_result: The README and the release state say plainly that main carrying the repairs and the public preview.2 wheel are different artefacts.
expected_automatic_behavior: the integration receipt names the exact merged commit and the unchanged preview.2 tag
expected_manual_behavior: the user is told which artefact to download for which capability
negative_behavior: a merged main must never be described as if the published wheel already contained the repairs
failure_recovery: state the gap and point at the next preview gate
